lines: It's the first morning of the summer holidays.
Since MegaMart opened across the street, fewer and fewer people visit your family's little corner shop.

lines.speaker: mom
lines.text: Morning, sweetheart. Try not to worry Dad today. The shop rent is due on Day 7 and things are... tight.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Psst! Grandpa has an old pushcart in the garage. We could sell stuff in the park and help!

events.speaker: grandpa

effects.log: Grandpa gave you his old pushcart.
effects.memory: Grandpa gave us his old pushcart.

lines: Ah, my old pushcart! I sold snacks from it before your dad was born.
It's yours now. But remember the first rule of business:
Buy for less, sell for more - and always be fair to your customers.
Lin's Wholesale, down the road on the left, sells stock cheap. Then set up the cart in the park.

choices.label: Thanks, Grandpa! I'll take good care of it.
Do you really think we can save the shop?

events.speaker: grandpa
lines: One coin at a time. Big things are built from small, steady steps.

events.speaker: grandpa

effects.log: Grandpa warned you about Smiley Steve's trick.
effects.memory: Asked Grandpa before trusting a stranger's deal.

lines: Half price, cash only, no receipts, and it ends TODAY? Oh, I know that trick.
When I was young, a man sold me 'cheap' flour. Half of it was full of bugs! I lost a whole week's money.
If a deal is too good to be true, it usually is. Always check what you're buying.

lines.text: When you look back towards the park, Smiley Steve's van has already gone.

events.speaker: mrs_lin
lines: Welcome to Lin's Wholesale! Shops buy from me in bulk, then sell to their own customers.
What you pay me is your COST PRICE. What you charge your customers is your SELLING PRICE.
The difference is your PROFIT - if you get it right!

events.speaker: mrs_lin
lines: Back again? Let's see what you need today.

events.speaker: dad
lines: Hey, kiddo. Quiet day at the shop again.

events.speaker: dad

events.speaker: dad
lines: Rent's paid thanks to you two. Now let's work out how to win our customers back from MegaMart.

events.speaker: mom
lines: A tip from your mom: before you buy anything, ask yourself - is it a NEED or a WANT?
Rent and food are needs. Sweets and toys are wants. Needs come first!

events.speaker: mom
lines: Home already? It's still light out.

choices.label: Yes, I'll call it a day.

lines: Inside the corner shop, the shelves are full but there are no customers.
You can hear MegaMart's cheerful music from across the street.
MegaMart is huge, bright and busy. A sign says: BISCUITS - 5 COINS A PACKET.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Five coins? That's more than Mrs. Lin charges US. How do they make people pay that?

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Maybe because it's easy. Everything is in one place.

lines: At dinner, you notice the cart money box is lighter than it should be.
Maya admits she took 5 coins from the cart money to buy sweets for her friends.

choices.label: Shout at her: "That was OUR money!"
Ask her why she did it.

events.speaker: mom

lines: Earlier that day, at the park...

Maya's face felt hot. She just wanted them to stop laughing.
So she took 5 coins from the money box and bought sweets for everyone.
It worked - for about a minute. Then she felt sick inside. She knew it was wrong.
All through dinner she was scared you would never trust her again.

events.speaker: maya
lines: ...The big kids said we were poor. I just wanted them to stop.

events.speaker: grandpa
lines: Did you know there's a market square at the end of our road? Just walk east along the street.

A stall at the festival... now THAT would help the family.
The market square is busy with stalls, music and the smell of fresh bread.

lines.text: Look at all the people! There must be ten times more customers here than in the park.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: That man by the purple building looks like he's in charge.

A sign on the empty stall says: STALL FOR RENT - ask Mr. Okafor at the Market Office.

A stall for the season costs 60 coins. And each day you open, there's a 5 coin fee for cleaning and lights.
Many more people walk through here than through the park. But it isn't cheap!

events.speaker: okafor

lines.text: I'm proud of you.

Or you can BORROW: a loan gives you money now, and you pay it back - plus interest - a little every week.

lines.text: It smells like summer!

lines: Did you see?! MegaMart put up a GIANT sign: LEMONADE - ONLY 2 COINS!

lines.speaker: dad
lines.text: We didn't open a second shop this time. Growing too fast can sink a business - knowing when to wait is smart too.

lines.text: One good shop, well run, beats two shops run badly.

lines: The summers pass. The pushcart gets a fresh coat of paint, then another.
The children grow up. The shops change. The town grows around them.
Twenty years go by...
It's the first morning of the summer holidays. You are ten years old.
Your parent runs the corner shop now - the same shop they once saved with an old pushcart.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Happy first day of summer! I've got something for you.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: This pushcart was your great-grandpa's. Then it was mine. Now it's yours.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: And I've put a little money from the family fund in your pocket - plus a savings account at the Town Bank. Use them wisely.

effects.memory: Got the old family pushcart - with cousin Nia.

lines.text: Cousin Nia joined your team. The family's friends are all grown up now - go and say hello around town.

events.speaker: parent
lines: Big news: the 100th Summer Festival is on Day 14! The town council wants every family to give something back to the town.

lines: How's the saving going? You need 40 coins for your project before the festival on Day 14.

lines: Well, well! Another one with that pushcart!

events.speaker: aunt_maya
lines: When I was little I took 5 coins from the cart money. Your parent made me pay back every coin.
I was SO cross. But it taught me that business money isn't pocket money. Fair is fair.

events.speaker: aunt_maya
lines: Your parent and I spent every summer at that pushcart. We argued about EVERYTHING.
But we always came back to the cart the next morning. That's what family is.

lines: Day 15. The festival bunting comes down, and grey clouds roll in over the town.

lines.text: Rainy days are quiet days for an outdoor business. People stay at home, and the pushcart sells less.

lines.speaker: parent
lines.text: Inside a shop, the rain hardly matters. Keep an eye on the sky at the top of the screen.

events.speaker: parent
lines: Every business has bad days. A storm, a broken wheel, a week of rain. The question is: who pays when it happens?
If the pushcart broke, the repair would cost about 30 coins. There are three ways to plan for that.
Insurance: you pay a little every week - 2 coins - and if the pushcart breaks, the insurance company pays for the repair.
An emergency fund: you keep 30 coins in your savings at the Town Bank, and you only touch them if something goes wrong.
Or you do nothing, and hope. Lots of people do. What do you think?

choices.label: An emergency fund - 30 coins in my savings.

effects.log: Your plan: keep 30 coins in savings at the Town Bank for emergencies.
effects.memory: Started an emergency fund.

lines: Good. You'll pay those 2 coins every week, even when nothing breaks. That's the deal with insurance.
